subject.title: Improve context overflow error message with specifics

question: What user-visible context-overflow diagnostic fields may OpenClaw show, and what privacy-safe session or channel label should be used instead of raw IDs?
rationale: The code can already compute or store much of the requested budget data, but the final message format and identifier redaction policy affect privacy and cross-channel UX and should be set by maintainers before automation changes user-visible errors.

options.title: Approve privacy-safe diagnostics
options.body: Show provider/model, effective budget, observed or estimated token count, overage, and a redacted display label when available, while keeping raw session keys and private IDs out of normal user-visible text.

options.title: Keep details in logs/status only
options.body: Leave error replies generic and direct users to status or diagnostics surfaces for token/session details, reducing privacy risk but leaving this issue's core UX request unresolved.

options.title: Defer to broader context visibility
options.body: Fold this into a wider context-pressure visibility design instead of changing overflow errors now, accepting continued generic failure messages in the meantime.

recommendation.title: Approve privacy-safe diagnostics
recommendation.body: Show provider/model, effective budget, observed or estimated token count, overage, and a redacted display label when available, while keeping raw session keys and private IDs out of normal user-visible text.

likelyOwner.reason: The current affected branches and previous review history point to steipete as the strongest recent owner for the agent-runner and auto-reply error UX decision.
